recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-20628 unless a future work group decision changes Procedure.category again.
issue_request: FHIR-20628 is a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request, voted 7-0-0 and applied for R5, asking that Procedure.category be changed to 0..* to support multiple axes of categorization. The issue description originally said Condition.category, but the reporter corrected that typo in the first comment and the resolution states Procedure.category.
initial_application: The Jira application comment links merge commit 88c604c66b028201ee797438b5154f3366ee7ec0. Its second parent, cff3828142337a515ea4a2fe0e509120467d8f0f, is titled 'GF#20628 Procedure.category 0..*...' and updated the historical Procedure spreadsheet. The 2021 source rework/conversion commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 preserved the GF#20628 committee note and max * cardinality in source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml.
additional_context: Procedure is listed as an active resource in source/fhir.ini, making source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml a current build-scoped source file. Current source lines 265-273 show Procedure.category with min 0 and max *, and v5.0.0 source lines 298-306 show the same. A later Patient Care WG Zulip thread explains that R4/R4B stayed at 0..1 and that the change was fixed in R5. Confluence searches found no conflicting FHIR-20628 decision. FHIR-7644 is an older DSTU1-era same-topic request that was Resolved - No Change and is background superseded by the later Published FHIR-20628 decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source files were modified because the current active Procedure StructureDefinition already implements the requested cardinality.
